name: Cai

attributes.attribute: first Brehon or judge in Ireland
also known as the Arthurian Kay

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cai is an Irish hero. The tradition names him as the first Brehon, or judge, in Ireland. He belonged to the Milesians, the people who came to Ireland. He was educated in Egypt. There he learned the law of Moses. He helped arrange the marriage of Mil to the pharaoh's daughter, Scota. At the time of the great flood he went with Moses into the desert. He later left Moses and rejoined his own kin. He then served as a judge for the people who reached Ireland. This figure is also known as Kay, a hero of the court of Arthur.

okr.objective: Cai is the first judge of Ireland in legend.
key_results: The record of the tale makes Cai the first brehon in Ireland.
He was a Milesian and studied in Egypt.
In the flood he went with Moses to the desert.
He became a judge for the people who reached Ireland.
He is identified with the Arthurian knight Kay.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
